findings.explanation: escapeDomain replaces only the first dot. With domains ['pay.example.co.uk'] the later dots stay unescaped wildcards, so origin 'https://pay.example-co.uk' matches. 'example-co.uk' is a registrable domain an attacker can own, so an attacker-controlled origin is allowed and reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

Lines 'a=x' followed by 'a.__proto__.__proto__.polluted=yes' make the traversal reach the existing string value 'x'. 'x'['__proto__'] yields String.prototype and String.prototype['__proto__'] yields Object.prototype, so the write at line 9 sets Object.prototype.polluted.

The m flag makes ^ and $ match at line breaks, so a sort such as 'name
<arbitrary SQL>' passes the test because its first line matches. The raw second line is then appended to ORDER BY unparameterised instead of the function throwing.

Math.trunc(amount * 100) under-counts when the float product lands just below an integer. For amount 19.99, 19.99 * 100 is 1998.9999999999998, so toPence returns 1998 rather than 1999 and splitAmount sums to the wrong total.
hasMore tests end < items.length - 1 instead of end < items.length. collectAll(['a','b','c'], 2) gets hasMore false on page 1, so it returns ['a','b'] and drops 'c'.

When the user has a string role, rolesOf returns that string and includes performs substring matching. A user with role 'superowner' passes hasRole(user, 'owner'), so canManageBilling returns true for a non-owner. The contract requires exact equality.

deposit adds amount to balance without checking that the result is a safe integer. With balance 9007199254740990 and amount 10 it returns 9007199254741000, breaking the guarantee that balance stays a safe integer.

Only a leading '//' is rejected. next = '/\evil.example' starts with '/' and not '//', so it is returned. The WHATWG parser treats backslash as a slash for http(s), so it resolves to https://evil.example/, outside app.example.
